_README: CURATED CONFIG -- intended for domain-expert review, deliberately kept out of code.
Each axis groups DrugBank category strings that all denote the SAME additive adverse
direction of effect. Channel B fires when 2+ drugs in a combination share an axis,
regardless of whether they share any protein -- this is what catches organ-level
convergence (e.g. the ACE-inhibitor + diuretic + NSAID 'triple whammy' renal risk),
which the shared-protein channel is structurally blind to.
SELECTION CRITERIA (what makes something an axis vs. not):
1. Denotes an ADVERSE direction of effect, not a therapeutic class.
'Nephrotoxic agents' YES. 'Cardiovascular Agents' (522 drugs) NO -- that is a
therapeutic class; two cardiovascular drugs sharing it implies nothing additive.
2. Plausibly ADDITIVE -- more drugs on the axis means more risk.
3. Sane population size. Very large categories carry little information.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: CYP inhibitor/inducer categories (those are mechanism, handled
by Channel A -- including them here would double-count the same finding), receptor-level
pharmacology classes ('Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Antagonists' -- mechanism, not outcome),
and vague catch-alls ('Toxic Actions').
'tiers' optionally maps a category to a severity-of-contribution label that DrugBank
itself provides. This is DrugBank's own grading of the drug's contribution to that axis;
it is NOT a clinical severity grade for the interaction.
To add an axis: confirm it meets all 3 criteria above, use the EXACT DrugBank category
string (see data/processed/drug_categories.jsonl), and write a plain-English consequence.

axes.label: QT prolongation
axes.consequence: additive QT-interval prolongation, raising the risk of torsades de pointes

axes.label: serotonergic burden
axes.consequence: additive serotonergic activity, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome
categories: Serotonergic Drugs Shown to Increase Risk of Serotonin Syndrome

axes.label: kidney injury
axes.consequence: additive strain on renal function, raising the risk of acute kidney injury

axes.label: raised potassium
axes.consequence: additive elevation of serum potassium, raising the risk of hyperkalemia

axes.label: bleeding risk
axes.consequence: additive impairment of clotting, raising the risk of bleeding

axes.label: muscle toxicity
axes.consequence: additive muscle toxicity, raising the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis

axes.label: anticholinergic burden
axes.consequence: additive anticholinergic load (confusion, urinary retention, constipation, falls)

axes.label: liver injury
axes.consequence: additive hepatic strain, raising the risk of liver injury

axes.label: bone-marrow suppression
axes.consequence: additive bone-marrow suppression, raising the risk of cytopenias

axes.label: lowered seizure threshold
axes.consequence: additive lowering of the seizure threshold

axes.label: slowed heart rate
axes.consequence: additive slowing of heart rate, raising the risk of symptomatic bradycardia

axes.label: low blood pressure
axes.consequence: additive blood-pressure lowering, raising the risk of symptomatic hypotension

axes.label: neuromuscular blockade
axes.consequence: additive neuromuscular blockade, raising the risk of respiratory weakness
